content: The primary analysis for the study is conducted at 72 weeks, as this time point includes the largest number of participants, which enhances the precision of the results. However, a limitation at this time point is the relatively short post-treatment follow-up for participants in the standard-of-care (SOC) arm, which may lead to an underestimation of relapse rates in the comparator group. Sensitivity analyses will be performed at 108 weeks (approximately 24 months), which corresponds to the follow-up period for a trial-specified secondary outcome. The population under study includes individuals with multidrug-resistant or rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis (MDR/RR-TB) and pre-extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis (pre-XDR-TB), regardless of fluoroquinolone resistance. The intervention involves the TB PRACTECAL BPaLM regimen (24 weeks), and the comparator is the TB PRACTECAL BPaL 600-300 regimen (24 weeks). Stratified analyses will be conducted for each regimen. In the WHO IPD dataset, most patients are treated for at least 18 months. The PRACTECAL study has a larger number of participants completing 72 weeks of follow-up compared to later time points. This may result in a slight underestimation of death or relapse rates in the PRACTECAL arm. Extending follow-up beyond this time would reduce statistical power. Sensitivity analyses will also be conducted at 24 months (108 weeks). The primary analysis for comparisons involving the BPaLM regimen will be conducted at 12 months to allow sufficient time for post-treatment relapse to occur. However, the smaller number of participants completing 12 months of follow-up in the PRACTECAL regimen may reduce the precision of estimates compared to the 6-month post-treatment follow-up. For the PRACTECAL study, the proportion of participants reaching 108 weeks (>24 months) is small, which reduces the precision of estimates for this population. Sensitivity analyses will be performed at 6 months and 108 weeks to account for the full follow-up period, despite the smaller cohort size. The primary analysis for comparisons involving the South African 2019 short-course regimen will be conducted at 72 weeks, as this time point includes the largest number of participants in the intervention arm, improving precision. Sensitivity analyses will also be performed at 108 weeks (24 months) and 12 months. For the NEXT study, the primary analysis will be conducted at 72 weeks, allowing for follow-up beyond the treatment period for the NEXT intervention regimen. Sensitivity analyses will be performed at 12 and 24 months of follow-up to include the full follow-up period for PRACTECAL, despite the smaller cohort size. In the PRACTECAL study, the 72-week and 108-week follow-up data include fewer participants than the 24-week cohort. The primary analysis for this question will be conducted at 18 months (72 weeks) to include most participants in the NIX and ZENIX studies. Sensitivity analyses will also be performed at treatment completion and 108 weeks. The primary analysis for comparisons involving the WHO long-IPD 2021 regimen will be conducted at 12 months. Sensitivity analyses will be performed at 6 months and 24 months. Participants who only reach 24 weeks will be censored at that date and excluded from subsequent follow-up analyses. For the South African 2017 short-course regimen, the primary analysis will be conducted at 72 weeks, as this time point includes the largest number of participants in the intervention arm, improving precision. Sensitivity analyses will also be performed at 108 weeks (24 months) and 12 months. The primary analysis for comparisons involving the BPaL regimen from the PRACTECAL, NIX, and ZENIX studies will be conducted at 12 months to include most participants. Sensitivity analyses will be performed at 6 months and 24 months.
